messages:
Kayla: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing an adaptive tiling + prefetch heuristic for the kernel autotuner. TL;DR: dynamically split large batches into seq-len tiles and prefetch KV shards for long-tail chats to reduce tail latency. Posting a config sketch and plan. Thoughts?

Mike: high level sounds promising. Biggest risk is memory pressure from prefetching. We need a robust eviction / budget mechanism and a default conservative cap. @Kayla can you include a safety cap? :thinking_face:

Ash: Agree with Mike. Also prefer async prefetch streams to avoid blocking compute. Have we measured prefetch overhead vs memcpy cost on A100/80GB?

Jordan: ran small experiment last month — for mixed traffic with 1% long seqs, prefetch lowered p95 by ~6–9% but increased max memory by ~3%. Will dig up numbers and attach.

Kayla: sharing a quick config sketch below (pseudo):
```
{
  "tiling": "seqlen_kmeans",
  "k": 4,
  "prefetch_shards": 2,
  "prefetch_budget_ratio": 0.15,
  "prefetch_evict_policy": "lru_local",
  "tile_threshold_tokens": 512
}
```
Would default to conservative values and require opt-in feature flag for rollout.

Lina: question — how do we pick `k`? K-means can be noisy in production. I'd prefer percentile-based buckets for stability (e.g., 50/90/99 cut points).

Mike: we tried silhouette-driven k before; it was unstable across workloads. Percentile bucketing (configurable percentiles) gave consistent behavior. Maybe do hybrid: offline kmeans to propose initial cutpoints, then switch to percentile thresholds online.

Jordan: another tradeoff — tiling breaks the continuity that benefits KV cache locality. If we split a batch, the KV cache may not be effective across tiles, adding cache-miss penalty. Need the estimator to account for that.

Kayla: agreed. propose a decision policy: only tile when estimated_speedup(tile_split) > estimated_cache_miss_penalty * safety_factor. That requires a lightweight runtime perf model (latency per seqlen, mem footprint, cache miss penalty).

Ash: we already have a micro estimator in the existing autotune path (latency_by_seqbin + mem_by_seqbin). We can extend it to estimate cache_miss_penalty by measuring local prefetch hit rates in offline runs.

sre-bot: incident: note that a prior rollout of eager prefetching caused OOMs on prod-1 two weeks ago. Recommend strict canary (5%), hard caps, and per-GPU budget metrics before broad rollout.

Mike: +1 to canary and hard caps. Also add fail-open so if estimator fails we revert to existing batching. :thumbsup:

Kayla: rollout plan suggestion — implement behind feature gate, metrics to collect: `prefetch_hits`, `prefetch_evictions`, `tile_split_count`, `estimator_mispred_rate`, `per_gpu_prefetch_bytes`. Canary 5% for 48h, then 25% for 72h, roll forward if no regressions.

Jordan: one more note: batching shape recommendations should be model-specific. Small transformers with shallow layers prefer different tile sizes than 70B models. Config should allow `model_tag` overrides.

Kayla: yep — config supports `model_tags` overrides and per-deployment `prefetch_budget_ratio`. Documentation and console visibility required (show per-deployment budget usage).

Lina: also add an opt-out at route level for latency-sensitive routes (we don't want tiling to touch sync RPCs).

Mike: I can own canary orchestration + alert rules. Kayla, can you draft the RFC follow-up note that includes the estimator equations and the probe test plan?

Kayla: will do. Action items: Kayla implements code + RFC note; Jordan runs bench jobs and shares numbers; Ash integrates estimator; Mike runs canary and alerting; Lina updates docs/console. Thanks all.
